categories.name: Claude
categories.description: Cache and temporary data from the Claude desktop app. Your conversations and settings are kept; caches are rebuilt on next launch.

categories.name: ChatGPT
categories.description: Cache files from the ChatGPT desktop app, rebuilt automatically as you use it.

categories.name: Cursor
categories.description: Cursor's render and code caches. Settings, extensions, and projects are untouched; caches regenerate on next launch.

categories.name: VS Code
categories.description: VS Code caches, logs, and cached extension data. Settings, extensions, and your projects are untouched.

categories.name: Ollama Models
categories.description: Downloaded AI models. Deleting means re-downloading many gigabytes per model — only clear this if you no longer use Ollama.

categories.name: Comet Browser
categories.description: Comet's cache and site storage. Clearing site storage can sign you out of websites; pages load slower on first visit afterward.

categories.name: Microsoft Edge
categories.description: Microsoft Edge's cache and site storage. Clearing site storage can sign you out of websites; pages load slower on first visit afterward.

categories.name: Firefox
categories.description: Firefox's disk cache. History and logins are unaffected; pages load slower on first visit afterward.

categories.name: Brave Browser
categories.description: Brave's disk cache. History and logins are unaffected; pages load slower on first visit afterward.

categories.name: Discord
categories.description: Discord's cached images and media, rebuilt as you use Discord.

categories.name: Xcode DerivedData
categories.description: Xcode's build intermediates and indexes. Safe to delete — the next build of each project is slower while Xcode rebuilds them.

categories.name: Xcode Archives
categories.description: Archived builds (.xcarchive) with debug symbols. You need these to symbolicate crash reports from shipped versions — keep archives for apps you've released.

categories.name: iOS Simulators (removes stale devices)
categories.description: Simulator devices and their data. The size shown covers all simulators, but cleaning only removes stale/unavailable ones via simctl.

categories.name: Xcode Cache
categories.description: Xcode's general caches and Interface Builder support files, regenerated automatically.

categories.name: npm Cache
categories.description: npm's download cache of package tarballs. The next install re-downloads what it needs; nothing in your projects changes.

categories.name: Yarn Cache
categories.description: Yarn's download cache. The next install re-downloads what it needs; nothing in your projects changes.

categories.name: pnpm Store
categories.description: pnpm's shared package store. Existing node_modules keep working; future installs re-download packages.

categories.name: Homebrew Cache
categories.description: Downloaded bottles and old formula versions. Homebrew re-downloads on demand; installed software is untouched.

categories.name: pip Cache
categories.description: Cached Python package downloads. pip re-downloads on the next install.

categories.name: CocoaPods
categories.description: Cached pod specs and downloads, re-fetched on the next pod install.

categories.name: Cargo Cache
categories.description: Rust registry caches and git checkouts. Re-downloaded on the next cargo build; installed binaries are untouched.

categories.name: Go Build Cache
categories.description: Go's compiled-object cache, rebuilt on the next go build.

categories.name: Go Module Cache
categories.description: Downloaded Go module sources shared by all your Go projects. Cleaned with go clean -modcache; the next build re-downloads dependencies.
categories.cleanCommand: export PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin"; go clean -modcache >/dev/null 2>&1 || { chmod -R u+w "$HOME/go/pkg/mod" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$HOME/go/pkg/mod"; }

categories.name: Gradle Caches
categories.description: Gradle's dependency and build caches. The next build re-downloads dependencies and recompiles, which can take a while.

categories.name: JetBrains IDEs
categories.description: Caches, indexes, and logs for IntelliJ-family IDEs. Projects and settings are untouched, but IDEs re-index on next launch — slow for big projects.

categories.name: Android Studio
categories.description: Android SDK cache and emulator images (AVDs). Deleting AVDs removes your configured emulators and their data.

categories.name: Docker (prune unused)
categories.description: Space Docker reports as reclaimable: stopped containers, dangling images, unused networks, and build cache. Cleaned with docker system prune — volumes are kept.
categories.scanCommand: export PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin"; docker system df --format '{{.Reclaimable}}' 2>/dev/null | awk '{v=$1; if (v ~ /GB$/) {sub(/GB$/,"",v); s+=v*1048576} else if (v ~ /MB$/) {sub(/MB$/,"",v); s+=v*1024} else if (v ~ /kB$/) {sub(/kB$/,"",v); s+=v} else if (v ~ /B$/) {sub(/B$/,"",v); s+=v/1024}} END {if (s>0) printf "%.0f\tdocker\n", s}'

categories.name: Old Virtualenvs (>90d)
categories.description: Python virtualenvs in your project folders untouched for 90+ days. Recreate one any time with pip install -r requirements.txt.

categories.name: node_modules (projects untouched >1yr)
categories.description: node_modules folders in projects that haven't been touched in over a year. Restore any time with npm install.
categories.scanCommand: find {PROJECT_ROOTS} -name node_modules -maxdepth 5 -type d 2>/dev/null | while read nm; do parent=$(dirname "$nm"); if [ -n "$(find "$parent" -maxdepth 0 -mtime +365 2>/dev/null)" ]; then du -sk "$nm" 2>/dev/null; fi; done | sort -rn | head -20

categories.name: node_modules (all, for reference)
categories.description: Every node_modules folder in your project folders, including active ones. Shown for size reference only — Featherweight will not delete these, because removing an active project's dependencies breaks its build.

categories.name: Large Files (>100MB, >30d)
categories.description: Files over 100 MB in Desktop, Downloads, and Documents not modified in 30+ days. These are your own files — review the list in the clean log; they go to the Trash.

categories.name: Old Downloads (>30d)
categories.description: Everything in your Downloads folder older than 30 days. These are your own files — they go to the Trash, and every removal is recorded in the clean log.

categories.name: App Leftovers
categories.description: Folders in ~/Library/Application Support whose app no longer appears to be installed — data orphaned by uninstalled apps. Detection uses Spotlight and can misfire for command-line tools, plugins, or apps installed outside /Applications, so Featherweight shows this for reference only and never cleans it automatically. Review each folder in Finder before deleting anything by hand.

categories.name: iMessage Attachments
categories.description: Photos, videos, and files received in Messages. Deleting removes them from your message history on this Mac; they may re-download from iCloud.

categories.name: Mail Downloads
categories.description: Attachments Mail downloaded for offline viewing. Mail fetches them from the server again when you reopen the message.

categories.name: Trash
categories.description: Everything currently in your Trash. Cleaning empties it permanently — this is the one category that can't be undone, because the files are already in the Trash.

categories.name: System Caches
categories.description: The contents of ~/Library/Caches — every app's scratch space. Apps rebuild caches as needed, so first launches may be slower. Other cache categories above are already excluded from this total.

categories.name: System Logs
categories.description: Crash reports and diagnostic logs. Only useful if you're actively debugging a problem.

categories.name: iOS Device Support
categories.description: Debug symbols Xcode extracted from every iOS version you've plugged in. Xcode re-extracts them on the next device connection — several minutes per device — and deleting mid-session can break debugging.

categories.name: Time Machine Snapshots (est.)
categories.description: Local Time Machine snapshots stored on this disk. The size is a rough estimate — macOS doesn't report exact snapshot sizes. Cleaned with tmutil; backups on your external Time Machine drive are untouched.
categories.scanCommand: n=$(tmutil listlocalsnapshots / 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'com.apple.TimeMachine'); if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then printf '%s\ttm-snapshots\n' "$((n * 500000))"; fi

categories.name: iOS Backups
categories.description: Local iPhone/iPad backups stored on this Mac. Deleting means you can't restore a device from them — make sure the device is backed up to iCloud first.

categories.name: QuickLook Thumbnails
categories.description: Preview thumbnails macOS generated for Quick Look, regenerated on demand.
